subject: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@arbortech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the performance-related gates we heard from your team and propose a concise acceptance checklist so we can keep momentum toward a POC.

Key SLOs you flagged during the call:
- Streaming latency (token-by-token): p95 <= 200ms for short-turn prompts (<=256 tokens)
- Non-streaming generation: p95 end-to-end <= 350ms for average prompt (<=512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: 60 concurrent streams / 120 QPS mixed workloads with 512-token avg
- Cold-start warm-up: first-request tail p99 <= 2.5s
- KV/cache retention: support for prefix caching across user sessions (per-session cache TTL ~30m)

Unresolved items I flagged for follow-up:
1) Traffic shape during business hours vs. batch (you mentioned 10x delta between peak and baseline). Can you share the 24-hour QPS distribution sample?
2) Encryption/KMS requirements for private deployment (you said SOC2 + customer-managed KMS for PII)
3) Success criteria for the POC (we proposed SLO + qualitative correctness checks)

Next steps I propose (short timeline):
- Ben: deliver a draft SLO acceptance checklist and demo-specific MAP by EOD tomorrow (attachment)
- Rishi: scope Dedicated capacity / config options and expected cost delta by Tue (cc'd)
- Elena: share your 24-hour traffic sample and confirm any additional streaming constraints

Attachments: demo_performance_notes.pdf (screenshots + token breakdown), slo_acceptance_checklist.xlsx (draft)

If that aligns, we can lock the POC scope and route an internal pricing proposal.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@arbortech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@arbortech.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up

Hi Ben,

Thanks — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications:
- Streaming p95 target: we'd prefer <=180ms if feasible; 200ms is acceptable for the POC but we'd want to see a path to 150ms in long-term plan.
- Concurrency: 60 concurrent streams is our baseline target; spikes can reach 250 for short periods during launches. We need graceful degradation (fallback to lower-fidelity model) rather than whole-service throttling.

I'll upload the 24-hour sample to the Drive folder by EOD and confirm KMS details with security (they require CMK in AWS KMS).

Elena
Director, Platform
ArborTech
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@arbortech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up

Elena — excellent notes, thanks. Updated plan below with decision criteria and owners; also calling out how we intend to measure SLOs during the POC.

POC measurement approach (high level):
- Synthetic harness that replays your 24-hr shape + isolated spike tests (we'll run on dedicated pool)
- Streaming instrumentation: token-level timestamps captured at ingress/egress to compute per-token latency p50/p95/p99
- Gradual concurrency ramp: start at 10 -> 60 -> 120 -> 250 for short bursts; confirm graceful fallback at each step

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- Metric: streaming p95 <= 200ms across baseline (acceptance) and <=180ms for stretch goal
- Metric: generation p95 <= 350ms
- Graceful degradation validated: fallback model maintains correctness >80% for degraded cases
- Throughput validated: maintain 60 concurrent streams for 8-hour window with <1% error rate
- Security: CMK integration verified; audit logs accessible via your SIEM

Owners & timing:
- Ben: finalize SLO checklist + submit POC order (today)
- Rishi: present config options (Dedicated vs Dedicated+burst) + cost delta (Tue 6/23)
- Laura: coordinate engineering trial window and test harness access (Wed 6/24)
- Elena: confirm KMS + upload traffic sample (Tue 6/23)

I'll attach the SLO spreadsheet and a short demo recording. If you agree, we'll spin up the test pool next week and schedule a 60-min run with your platform team.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: slo_acceptance_checklist.xlsx, demo-recording-20260621.mp4
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up

Ben — added capacity/config notes and an initial cost sketch. Key tradeoffs:
- Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) with auto-burst to shared for spikes: predictable latency, higher baseline cost, supports 250 short spikes.
- Quantized model variant reduces per-token CPU/GPU but may increase p95 by ~10-12ms for streaming; good fallback when tails are acceptable.

Initial cost sketch (monthly, rough):
- Dedicated baseline (24/7): $27K
- Dedicated + burst (reserve + on-demand overflow): $34K
- Short-term POC (2 weeks, temporary ramp): ~$8K (tracking GPU hours)

I'll put a short doc in the Drive and flag the specific instance types.

-r
From: Elena Park <elena.park@arbortech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@arbortech.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance gates & demo acceptance criteria — ArborTech discovery follow-up

Ben / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We're aligned on the checklist for the POC except:
- Please aim for a streaming p95 <=190ms for the POC test runs if possible.
- We'll prioritize the CMK integration and upload the traffic sample today.

Let's go ahead and lock in the 2-week POC window starting Mon 6/29. Can you share an invite for the test kickoff and the acceptance criteria doc in Drive?

Elena

-- 
Elena Park
Director, Platform
ArborTech
notes: Thread contains demo follow-up, SLO checklist, pricing sketch and POC MAP. Internal owners: Ben (sales), Rishi (solutions/infra), Laura (product ops).
summary: Post-demo follow-up focused on performance SLOs (streaming and non-streaming latency targets), throughput/concurrency targets, graceful degradation strategy, CMK requirement, and agreement to run a 2-week POC starting 2026-06-29.
